title: ID0376219-DC/Si-D/FR[rhAYBP] - Missing converters in DC3/4
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
Converters are found (230V are supplied) but Fastshutdown is not possible
Root cause:
KF214 is faulty → 12V coming from the output when it should only come when it's in Emergency
Solution:
Replace KF214
On DAMEX Sanctioned List:
Siemens
Warranty Status:
Active

additional_info.subject: ID0376219-DC/Si-D/FR[rhAYBP] - Missing converters in DC3/4 CRM:00315001690
additional_info.body:
Hello Antoine,
After today's site visit with the assistance of the technician, we were able to find the root cause of the problem.
Here is a short summary of the performed actions:
As we checked yesterday, the converter grouping was not passing in DC3 and DC4 after the closing of the QA11-12.
As such I thought that one of the contactors might not be working correctly.
Not the case as we measured the continuity between A1 and A2 and we had continuity in both contactors.
As such, the next thought was, the converters were not powering on due to the fastshutdown signal being ON:
In XD39 we measured between 3B/3A and 1B/1A, to housing and had 12V (as it should).
But from the dispenser side, XD39 4D/4C and 2D/2C, we also had 12V, this is the indication that the StateMonitor is sending command to fastshutdown the converters in DC3 and DC4.
When we removed the XD39:4C and XD39:2C, the converter grouping was possible and successful without the fastshutdown check (unsuccessful)
With the connections still removed, the measured directly on the output of the StateMonitor, CCS-A OUT (J1) SuC and CCS-A OUT (J1) SuO:
And we found that there are 12V constantly toggled in the output of the StateMonitor
What could be the reason is that the internal switch/contactor might be damaged or welded and as such it always have 12V.
As such please order and replace this StateMonitor KF214.
I will send this ticket to the RC-FR queue please pick it up for replacement purposes. You can reach out to me for the meeting schedule in case you need further support.
Thank you for your help in translating and have a nice day :D
Best regards,
Francisco
